archetype.name: Playoff Team (defense-and-glass)
archetype.definition: A defending champion that is winning this year by choking off shots and owning the boards rather than through the high-powered offense that carried it last season, which gives it a contender's floor and a question mark on its ceiling.

report.headline: The champs have swapped identities: elite defense and rebounding, now an average offense
report.take:
New York is 11-6, eighth on the site, and has a 5.9 Net Rtg that ranks 7th. This is a different team from the one that won 53 games and 16 playoff games last season. That group had the 3rd-ranked offense and the 7th-ranked defense. This one has flipped the order: the defense ranks 4th with a 108.4 DRtg, six points better than the league average, while the offense ranks 14th at 114.3, exactly the league mean. The Knicks also play slower than almost anyone, at a 94.7 pace, which is why they rank only 26th in points scored per game even though they are a middle-of-the-pack offense per possession.

The season turns on two things: shot suppression and rebounding. Opponents post a 51.2 eFG % (5th) and shoot 63 % at the rim (8th). The Knicks force almost nothing, ranking 26th in Opp TOV %. That is sturdier than it sounds, because a defense built on contesting shots and then finishing the possession holds up better than one living on steals. The finishing is the strength: a 76.9 DRB % ranks 2nd and a 53.5 REB % ranks 2nd. Karl-Anthony Towns sits 4th on the center tab, with a 7.9 BPM, a 65 TS % and a +10.4 On-Off, and he is the reason the frontcourt grades A+.

The numbers hide a shaky offense and a soft middle of the roster. Team eFG % ranks 24th and FT Rate ranks 28th, so the offense depends on making threes, where the Knicks shoot 36.9 % (7th). Jalen Brunson carries a 32.4 USG % at a modest 55.8 TS %. The wings grade C-: Mikal Bridges has a 48.4 TS % and a -22.1 On-Off, and Josh Hart has a 42.5 TS %. Opposing small forwards take 24.3 % of the points scored against New York, against a league share of 19.9 %. Landry Shamet's 66.4 TS % and +26.3 On-Off have papered over a lot, and that kind of shooting rarely holds. The current five-game win streak is also thinner than it looks. It includes an overtime win in Toronto, 102-99 at Minnesota and 97-96 over Portland, and the margin over those five games is below the season rate.

The direction is still good. A 2-4 October gave way to a 9-2 November, and points allowed per game dropped from 107.67 to 100.82. The W vs Pt Diff of -1 says the record is, if anything, a touch behind the play. The pace number projects 53 wins, which matches last season. The open question is whether the offense climbs back toward last season's level once OG Anunoby and Miles McBride, both listed out, return. Until then, this is a top-eight team that wins ugly.

strengths.title: A shot-contesting top-five defense
strengths.body: The 108.4 DRtg ranks 4th and sits six points better than the league average. It comes from opponents' shooting, not from forcing turnovers: Opp eFG % is 5th and Opp Rim FG % is 8th. Defenses built on shot quality tend to hold up over a season, and this one improved sharply in November.

strengths.title: Owning both glasses
strengths.body: The Knicks rank 2nd in DRB % and 2nd in REB %, so opponents rarely get second shots after a contested miss. They also rank 6th in ORB %, which helps an offense that otherwise shoots poorly from two and rarely gets to the line. Rebounding has been a staple across their recent seasons (76.7 DRB % last year), so this is a real trait rather than a hot start.

strengths.title: Towns as the engine
strengths.body: Towns ranks 4th of 92 on his tab, with a 7.9 BPM, a 65 TS % and a +10.4 On-Off. He is the team's most efficient high-volume scorer and its main rebounder. The A+ frontcourt grade rests largely on him, which is a strength and also a single point of failure, especially with Anunoby out.

concerns.title: The offense lost its edge
concerns.body: Last season's 119.8 ORtg ranked 3rd; this year's 114.3 is merely league average. The Knicks are 24th in eFG % and 28th in FT Rate, so they live on threes. Brunson's 32.4 USG % at a 55.8 TS % is a heavy load at middling efficiency. The track record says some of this comes back, but not without healthier rotation pieces.

concerns.title: Wings are a weak spot
concerns.body: The wing group grades C-. Bridges has a 48.4 TS % and the roster's worst On-Off at -22.1, and Hart has a 42.5 TS %. Opposing small forwards take a far larger share of the scoring against New York than the league norm. This is the one group dragging on both ends of the floor.

concerns.title: Thin margins and missing bodies
concerns.body: The 5-0 run came with a smaller margin per game than the season rate, and it included an overtime win and two one-possession games. Anunoby, second in frontcourt minutes, and McBride are both listed out. Shamet's 66.4 TS % is propping up the guard rotation, and shooting that hot is the most likely number on the roster to cool.

trend.note: A 2-4 October turned into a 9-2 November, built mostly on defense: points allowed per game fell from 107.67 to 100.82. The latest five wins were narrower than the season norm, so the climb is real but the recent results flatter it slightly.

weekAhead.headline: Three home games against teams ranked below them
weekAhead.body:
New York plays Cleveland, Miami and Atlanta, all at home. All three sit below the Knicks on the site (12th, 13th and 11th) and all have a lower Net Rtg. The matchups are stylistically clear. Cleveland and Miami have top-seven offenses but defenses ranked 20th and 23rd. Atlanta mirrors New York, with a 7th-ranked defense and a 19th-ranked offense. Each of the three gives up plenty to opposing centers, which points the offense toward Towns.

The risks are Cleveland's offense, which beat New York 115-107 at the Garden earlier this month, and Atlanta's A+ wings against the Knicks' C- group. Atlanta also forces turnovers at the 3rd-highest rate, a test for a team that is only average at protecting the ball. Without Anunoby, a sweep is possible but two wins is the more honest expectation.

keyMatchups.title: Towns against leaky interiors
keyMatchups.body: Atlanta gives up the second-most points to centers in the league and ranks 26th in Opp Rim FG %. Cleveland is near the bottom in points allowed to centers as well. With Anunoby out, Towns should carry even more of the offense, and the matchups invite it.

keyMatchups.title: Cleveland's offense tests the defense
keyMatchups.body: Cleveland's 118.6 ORtg ranks 5th, and it already scored 115 on New York at home. The Cavs rarely turn it over and are 3rd in eFG %, so the Knicks' shot-contesting and rebounding defense faces its stiffest test of the week. Cleveland's D- wings are a spot where Bridges and Hart could finally find room.

keyMatchups.title: Guards' night against Miami
keyMatchups.body: Miami allows the most points in the league to shooting guards and ranks 28th in Opp 3P %. That suits a Knicks offense that ranks 7th in 3P %. It is a good spot for Shamet and Brunson to keep the scoring afloat.

weekAhead.watch: Whether the offense can hold up without Anunoby against Cleveland's scoring, or whether the Knicks need another tight, defense-first escape.

restOfSeason.body:
The defense and the rebounding look sustainable. They rest on shot quality and the glass, they echo a long rebounding track record, and Towns is playing at a top-five level at his position. The record is not inflated: W vs Pt Diff is -1, and the margin implies 12 wins against the actual 11. A pace of 53 wins is a fair midpoint. The offense should drift up from league average once Anunoby and McBride return, which would offset the expected cooling of Shamet's shooting.

What keeps this from being a clear top-three team is the wing play and an offense that depends on threes and does not get to the line. The Atlantic is crowded, with Philadelphia at 14-3 and Boston level at 11-6. Expect New York to settle near 50-plus wins with a top-five defense, unless the wings keep giving back what the frontcourt earns.
swingFactors: Whether Bridges and Hart find their shooting

confidence.note: Seventeen games is a small sample, but the defensive and rebounding signals are strong and consistent with the team's history.
